title: A missing summary delay excludes one human excitatory route with shorter two-edge onset sums in both clamp modes
abstract: We audited summary-delay coverage in paired current-clamp and voltage-clamp fits from Allen cortical slices. Seven mouse VisP routes and five human TCx routes had three excitatory connections with accepted fits in both modes. One human route had shorter two-edge onset sums in both modes, by 0.802 and 0.342 ms. A missing summary delay excludes this route from complete-summary analyses. Under the documented 0.1 ms start windows, all twelve route orders are fixed before optimization. The positive human route is lost when known excitatory cell labels are required. This is a coverage and fit-constraint audit, not evidence for faster indirect transmission. Relay spike time, biological delay error, and actual indirect responses were not measured. The small selected sample does not support a species comparison. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, hashes and external-data regeneration steps are supplied. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Complete-summary selection excludes two human routes, including the only one with a shorter two-edge onset sum. Both recording modes give the same order for every selected route. Counts describe dependent selected routes.
